sentences.text: At the outset, Shri Ali, learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the investigation, in the meantime, has been completed and the charge sheet has been filed.

He has further submitted that though the applicant is ready and willing to appear before the learned Court,
he apprehends that on such appearance, his prayer for bail may not be considered mainly for two reasons; firstly, the applicant has been stated to be an absconder in the charge sheet and secondly,
since the offence is Sessions triable, the learned Magistrate may not exercise the powers for consideration of bail.
Ms. Bhuyan, learned Addl. PP, however has submitted that if a prayer for bail is made, the learned Magistrate would consider the same in accordance with law.

The Full Bench of this Court in the case State of Assam Vs. State, reported in 2007 (1) GLT 330 has laid down that prior to an order of committal, the Magistrate may exercise the powers to consider a prayer for bail in accordance with law.

entities.text: State of Assam Vs. State, reported in 2007 (1) GLT 330
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the aspect of stating the applicant as an absconder in the charge sheet, that aspect may also be considered by the learned Magistrate in accordance with law, if good causes are able to be shown by the applicant.

In view of the above, the instant petition is closed by giving liberty to the applicant to appear and make a prayer for grant of bail which would be considered in accordance with law and in terms of the observations made above.
